title: Organizations the payment table shows paid far more than the nonprofit dataset does
question: For which organizations, and in which years, does the City’s table of every payment show much more than its nonprofit-spending dataset?
finding: In 122 organization-years at 35 organizations the payment table is higher than the nonprofit-spending dataset by a quarter and $1 million or more, fiscal 2019 to 2026. The largest differences over those years are Children's Council of San Francisco ($802.3 million), Delta Dental Plan of California ($508.0 million), Homebridge Inc ($237.8 million). The organization pages on this site use the dataset, so for these organizations they understate what the City paid; the contract titles in the last columns show what the extra money was paid under.
how: The dataset’s yearly total for each profiled organization is set beside the sum of every paid voucher to a payee with the same name in the same fiscal year. A row is listed when the payment table is higher by more than 25% and by at least $1.0 million. The three largest contract titles for that organization and year are printed with their amounts.
limits: The Controller’s description of the dataset says supplier payments “may include payments for services to the City, such as memberships, use of space, and passthrough payments to beneficiaries”, and that to count contracted services it keeps four types of goods and services only (community-based organization services, homeless housing and supportive services, and two kinds of professional and specialized services). Organizations are matched to payees by name, so a payee spelled differently is missed and the payment-table side is a floor. 4 payees that the payment table spells differently were tied to their organizations by contract number instead. A difference between two City tables is a fact about the tables and says nothing against the organization. Money an agency passes on to others (child-care subsidies paid to providers, for example) and premiums paid to an insurer are real City payments but are not what the organization spends on itself. The fiscal year in both tables is the Controller’s label, which is not always the year a payment was made: the payment table files some earlier payments under a later year. The two are compared label against label because the dataset follows the label: across the 2,622 contract-years where the label and the voucher number of the payments give different sums, the dataset matches the label sum to the dollar in 2,410 and the voucher-number sum in 121. A year shown here can therefore be later than the year the money was paid; in 3 of the 122 organization-years listed, $1.0 million or more of the payment-table figure carries a voucher number from an earlier year, the most being $35.7 million for Children's Council of San Francisco in fiscal 2025.
